# CANDIDATE: ZERO_DTE_PCR_OI_MEAN_REVERSION_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-08-24  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

When the 0DTE put/call open interest (PCR_OI) ratio deviates sharply from its intraday mean, dealer hedging imbalances tend to revert price toward VWAP, creating a long opportunity. This captures short-term mean reversion driven by options-flow dynamics not yet represented in the registry.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** If PCR_OI_0DTE (live) exceeds its 20‑bar rolling mean by 1.5 standard deviations for two consecutive 5‑minute bars, price is below VWAP by at least 0.1×ATR(5), and the EMA ribbon is bullish (EMA8 > EMA21 > EMA55), enter long at the close of the second bar.  
**Exit:** Initial stop at the lowest low of the prior three bars (chart‑stop). Take 50% of position at 1.5R. Trail the remainder with a 20% chandelier exit from the highest‑since‑entry price.  
**Regime filter:** Only active when VIX1D < 18 and time is between 09:45‑11:30 ET to avoid noisy open/close periods.

   - Max drawdown: Unknown pending backtest.  
   - Blow‑up scenario: Persistent dealer‑positioning imbalance that prevents mean reversion, leading to a series of stopped‑out trades.
